representative_examples.post_title: Need Advice – IIM Sambalpur vs Reattempting CAT
representative_examples.text: You have good academic scores and years at hand. I cannot stress enough how important the duration of work experience becomes for strategy (also product) roles. Moreover, admit into tier 3 b schools (new/baby IIMs etc.) makes NO SENSE at all in the current market. Heck, even the top b schools are struggling now to place their students at top firms. You are very unlikely to get your desired roles from IIM Sambhalpur. I would say, gain at least 2 years of wex and then write CAT again. You’re at 94, It is fairly easy to get 98/99 percentile in a couple of months’s prep.

representative_examples.post_title: Should i choose IIM Sambalpur
representative_examples.text: The only negative you have is not your age but your work ex cross 4 years but I have seen countless examples of people converting tier 1 bschools after 4 year work ex. Trust me, IIM sambalpur doesn't make sense for you at all. You may even consider isb or executive mba if not cat but definitely not sambalpur

representative_examples.post_title: Tier 1 MBA/PGP alumni (2 Year Full Time): how did the 28-30 year olds with non-traditional profiles fare at placements vs the rest of the batch? Unplaced numbers, salary gaps, real stories welcome.
representative_examples.text: If your intention is honest and you are willing to work hard ,no one can stop you. You will get all the support you need . There is a group run by IIML folks who provide mentorship to CAT aspirants.  In your case I can personally forward your case if you wish to . You will get benefitted. You can interact perhaps with folks of 28-30 years with gap years doing great in top tier MBA programs. I personally did my MBA at 32 years of age from IIT Roorkee, did exceptionally well . I had no guarantee for a good placement, regardless I worked hard and sincerely and I comfortably got placed in a middle management role in a good Organization. There is nothing called impossible in this world if you set your mind up to achieve your goals .

representative_examples.post_title: 9/8/8 GNEF, CAT 89.85%ile, Life Science background, Confused about MBA / gap / job, need advice
representative_examples.text:
If you convert Sambalpur, think about it, but your potential is still high. You can get a much better B-school, but the thing is, CAT is risky. If you don't prepare well this year, you might end up with 70s (percentile) next year. So, ask yourself: don't take a drop; that will only ruin your profile. Instead, go for some low-paying core job. Your main focus should be work experience, not money. It's better if you can shift and get a high-paying, good corporate job, but the thing is, you can't because of family responsibility.

I think you should talk to your parents once. If they are comfortable, then go for some good job outside. In the next 2-3 years, you will be happy about this decision.

If not, at least try a good quality WFH job (last option).

Your profile is very good; don't settle for less (but I saw people who messed up after taking a drop). So, make a mindset, then decide. Plus, give 3 hours every day to study consistently for the next 300-something days; you will definitely score well.

representative_examples.post_title: IIM sambalpur or repeat CAT. I know this is asked too many times but hear me out.
representative_examples.text: Your biggest mistake is to quit the job and prepare. The cushioning a job provides is gone . I am not saying your decision was entirely wrong ,many folks who have no idea how jobs work , how CAT and exam is do similar mistakes . Let's forget about ROI for now.  You converted Sambalpur with a just okay percentile, that means the interviewers saw something in you . There are hundreds of folks out there who would grab your seat if you give it up . That's a high level of competition. My only worry is , should you take an admit at S , that will you be able to withstand the rigour of it because job or no job at the end of the program,they will make life miserable for you in academics. IIMs are known for brutal rigour . Coming to placements, if you do your MBA properly, definitely you will do well , you will find a way to get your ROI , worrying about it will do you no good now . You first need to convince yourself what is it you want ? If you feel you are not ready for the rigour ,as well give it another shot next year . Whatever you do first convince yourself first.  I don't see any problem in taking an admit since you cleared the whole process.

representative_examples.post_title: IIM Sambalpur: Indian Institute of Mismanagement
representative_examples.text:
I feel as a soon-to-be alum of IIM Sambalpur, I should take the responsibility of clearing out some nuances and share my two cents on the situation here. 

Honestly, it's not as bad as it seems. Every system has its inefficiencies, but I'm confident that the institute will learn and improve 5-6 years down the line.

I've been to other colleges for events and tournaments, and I can say that the food here is actually pretty decent - at least it's edible and there's some variety!

Placements are a bit of a worry, especially with summer internships. But for final placements, things are looking up, the progress was stagnant in mid Dec to mid Jan. But post 2nd week of Jan, we've got multiple companies coming in every day, and the admin is focusing more on final placements this year because many well-reputed companies ditched last year for Finals after taking people from SIP which is kinda loss for the institution.

As for packages, the average is around 13-14 LPA. Just be realistic about your expectations - if you're dreaming of 20+ LPA, you should've done your research before joining.

You may not consider IIM Sambalpur as one of the top-tier IIMs, but for me, the experiences I've had here have been truly transforming. Through my involvement in clubs and committees, fests, events, workshops, and case competitions, I've learned and grown a lot It's been overall quite worthwhile experience that I'll always cherish.

Ultimately, it's your call. Just weigh the pros and cons and make an informed decision, and do enough research before you come. There'll be many posts for all the colleges now, mostly for clearing the waitlist, so beware.

All the best!

representative_examples.post_title: Should i choose IIM Sambalpur
representative_examples.text: From whatever I have read and your comments, it seems like you are more willing to join IIM Sambalpur than not do it . I can't comment on current economy because what I am seeing in terms of placements I haven't seen so far in my life . It's devestation on all fronts .Having said that , in my own experience, I took a risk like 20 years ago and after 8 years of work experience, I took up a 2 year MBA at DOMS IIT Roorkee . At that point in time ,everyone I went to for suggestions asked me not to join as there would be no surety of a decent placement. I though let's get it done with and I was totally committed to my MBA . I said to myself at worst I won't get a job , will manage . Gave my 100% to my MBA ,got a great CGPA , competing with a class where average age was like 21-22 and I was 32 . Made great friends with younger folks . Our batch was very good and 2 years thereafter we had stellar placements . I got a good Middle Management role and subsequently did well . Another aspect was lower fees .if I remember correctly I paid around 2 lacs for the whole program. So it's about your take on the situation. Good luck 👍

sample_documents.post_title: I completed 1 year at IIM Sambalpur, and now I’m building my own startup and making music. Ask Me Anything!
sample_documents.text:
# 1. Hostel, Mess (Food), and Staying Facilities

The staying facilities are quite comfortable. The mess food is decent, and they actually offer a pretty good menu. For accommodation, you get double sharing rooms, and you are paired with a student from your own course.

# 2. Interaction with Professors

Since the batch size is small (around 90 students per batch), the interaction with professors is very high, just as you'd expect. It is quite easy to approach, meet, and interact with the faculty members whenever needed.

# 3. Faculty (Tech vs. Management)

The faculty lineup is a balanced mix. There are dedicated tech professors as well as management professors, so you get the right expertise for both technical and business subjects rather than management faculty trying to teach core tech.

# 4. Coding and Placement Culture

The coding culture is still growing. Honestly, only a few people are heavily into core coding right now—myself and one of my friends are actively doing it and focusing on platforms like LeetCode and Kaggle. A good portion of the batch isn't as intensely focused on it yet.

# 5. Education Loan Process & Campus Banks

Yes, education loan facilities are readily available. Union Bank of India has a presence here to assist students. You don't necessarily have to get it done beforehand from home; you can easily get your loan processed through the bank branches that visit the campus during the orientation program. You just need to bring your official offer letter along.

sample_documents.post_title: Are the new/baby IIMs worth joining?
sample_documents.text:
Newer iims like jammu, bodh gaya, sirmaur, sambalpur have improving placements but significant gap versus old iims in alumni network, brand recognition, and median packages.Roi depends heavily on your alternatives and career goals.

Currently doing my pg at masters union and honestly if choice is between newer iim versus no mba or tier 3 college, newer iims are worth it.But if you can wait a year and improve cat score for older iims, that's often better long-term investment.
